$comment: D-CPP-LINE-DIRECTIVE-MACRO-OPERAND: C23 6.10.6p6 — a `# line pp-tokens` directive matching NEITHER literal form is PERMITTED; its operand is macro-expanded and the RESULT must then match one of them. At the pre-change HEAD every such directive died on `error[P_PreprocessorDirective]: #line requires a digit sequence — got: <macro name>` (✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI over a 32-shape probe corpus, later grown to 39 across all three references). FIVE ARMS, each scored 0 by a different plausible wrong implementation: (1) an OBJECT-LIKE macro expanding to the digit sequence, which an implementation that never expands scores 0 on; (2) ONE macro carrying BOTH the number and the quoted name, which an implementation expanding only the first operand token scores 0 on while passing arm 1; (3) a FUNCTION-LIKE macro whose `##` paste ASSEMBLES the digits, which a private one-token substituter scores 0 on because arity, argument pre-expansion and pasting belong to the ordinary expander; (4) RESCAN through a second macro with the name supplied by a third in the same directive; (5) ★ the SELF-REFERENTIAL `#line __LINE__` after an earlier `#line`, the only arm that fails toward a WRONG NUMBER rather than an error — the operand's `__LINE__` must read the mapping in effect BEFORE this directive, not the physical line and not the record being created. ✔MEASURED BY EXECUTION: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both build and RUN this to exit 42 under -std=c17 and -std=c2x alike, and MSVC 19.51.36252 accepts every shape. ANTI-FOLD: the score is multiplied by a runtime `argc` predicate so the release pipeline cannot reduce main to a constant return. Data-model-independent (int arithmetic and byte comparisons only), so the one exit code holds on all four targets and on the shipped release pipeline. exit = 8 + 8 + 8 + 9 + 9 = 42.
